_doc: Camera ETA check + IR position on the image + vision load. Built 2026-10-25 from OLD-unit runs (2026-10-24 14:39-15:52, before the CPR fix) because no new-unit run has camera data. ETA uses camera pixels and camera vu only, so the rpm units do not matter; real rpm = old rpm / 9 is given only as a label. PROVISIONAL: only 11 clean cycles.

camera_moved.how: operator said the camera never moved; snapshot 2026-10-25 20:36 (vision/snap_roi.png) shows the ROI saved 2026-10-22 in vision/vision_calibration.json still on the belt edges (u 93-608, v 196-281). No reference frame from 10-24 exists.

source.clean_cycle_rule: arriving cube seen moving (vu < -5 px/s, u < 320) in a camera/perception snapshot <= 0.6 s before belt/event ARRIVED; ARRIVED and arm/ir detected agree within 0.15 s
source.split: clean cycles in time order: even = find u_IR (6), odd = ETA test (5)

ir_u_px.note: u at ARRIVED, extrapolated from the last snapshot with u + vu*dt; belt axis u, dir -1 (cubes move toward smaller u). Slightly lower u at higher rpm = trigger/report latency of ~0.3 s.

camera_view.kalman_vu_warmup_s: about 3 s after a track appears (vu ramps 0 -> steady)

eta_error_s.definition: ETA = (u_IR - u) / v, error = ETA - actual time to ARRIVED (+ = predicted late)
eta_error_s.kind: 10 s with camera vu = SYSTEMATIC (cube only just entered the view at u 530-544, Kalman vu still -15..-20 instead of -28.6, ETA too late). 5 s = small, mostly random, slight early bias -0.4 s at 11.1 rpm. A steady/belt-prior speed removes the 10 s bias.

proposal.pass_rule: |ETA error| <= 1.0 s at 5 s look-ahead; use camera vu only after the track is >= 3 s old (hits >= ~30 at 6 fps), before that use the belt-encoder speed (predict.py prior)
proposal.wake_margin: rest -> home takes ~36 s but the camera sees a cube only ~13 s (12.6-20) before the IR, so waking from REST on a camera ETA cannot be on time. Waking is only possible from upstream info (feeder event / schedule). Supports O2 = hold home + brake belt. Margin for a short move (e.g. standby -> grip-ready) = move time + 1 s.

problems_found: 52 of 63 cubes have no camera track at the IR. In the 3 arm-speed runs the track ends at u ~247 about 3 s (2.9-3.6) BEFORE ARRIVED in every cycle -> most likely vision lag of ~3 s (frames queued). camera/perception ts is the publish time, not the frame capture time, so the lag is not measurable from the logs.

Fix proposal (needs OK, not done): vision_live_tracks.py publish_perception adds frame capture time (RealSense frame.get_timestamp() / time at wait_for_frames return) as ts_frame, plus processing lag.

rows.note: temp still rising at the end

rows.skipped: 15 fps already uses ~87-95 % of one core; 30 cannot keep up and would build the same frame lag

vision_load.note: D415 640x480 supports 6/15/30 fps only; lower than 6 means skipping frames in software. Pi system RAM available ~760 MB of 3.8 GB.
vision_load.staging_conclusion: Keep 6 fps (enough: ETA error at 5 s is within 1 s). Going higher costs ~2.3x CPU and +8-15 C. Dropping/pausing vision while the belt is stopped saves at most ~38 % of one core (~9.5 % of the Pi); worth it only if Pi power matters - Pi power itself was not measured.

waiting_for_machine: New-unit run with vision ON (20 rpm / arm 1.5 and 15 rpm / arm 1.5, >= 10 cycles each) to confirm u_IR and the ETA error at real rpm, with frame-capture timestamps
Check the ~3 s vision lag during arm motion (is it occlusion or lag?)
